key_insight: T3D teaches a diffusion language model to reproduce high-quality multi-step generation in only a few refinement steps by distilling its own decoding trajectories and directly optimizing for discriminative sequence quality.
problem_solved: Diffusion-based LLMs require many refinement steps for good text quality; reducing steps greatly impairs generation, limiting practical inference speed and latency.
method: Trajectory self-distillation: use the model's long-step generative trajectories as supervision so a compact few-step student mimics later trajectory states.
Direct discriminative optimization: incorporate sequence-level discriminative objectives (ranking/quality-aware loss) to align few-step outputs with high-quality long-step outputs.

Training recipe for few-step decoding: combine trajectory matching, reconstruction losses, and discriminative penalties to retain generation quality while enabling parallel multi-token decoding in very few steps.
impact: Enables much faster, parallel token generation from diffusion language models with minimal quality loss, making DLLMs viable for low-latency and resource-constrained deployment in production NLP systems.

paper_title: T3D: Few-Step Diffusion Language Models via Trajectory Self-Distillation with Direct Discriminative Optimization
paper_authors: Tunyu Zhang, Xinxi Zhang, Ligong Han, Haizhou Shi, Xiaoxiao He
